name: example-payments
description: A worked example corpus shipped with knowledge-as-code, holding the invented standards of a fictional payments system and consuming Example Engineering. It binds nobody.

components.note: Files an observation about the corpus as an issue on the repository that published it, reading corpus/manifest.json for the address. It names no type, so it travels with every bundle.

Asks the owner of a clause to accept a knowing departure from it, as an issue on the repository that published the corpus holding that clause. A clause is a standard's rule or a policy's clause, so it travels where the export carries either.

Answers a question from the corpus, reading each exported type through the reference file beside it, and fetches a record's published source through retrieval.md. kac bundle lists the trigger line of each reference file that travelled beside its description. It needs no type of its own, so it travels only where something it reads did.
Reads a rule from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl and the owning standard beside it. Lists the standards from views/build-index.md where that view survived.
Reads a clause from corpus/policies/clauses.jsonl and the owning policy beside it.
Reads a control from corpus/controls/ and says what checks a rule. A control declares no part, so there is no flat file and the record is the unit.
Reads a fix from corpus/fixes/ and says whether this problem has been solved here before. A fix declares no part, so there is no flat file and the record is the unit.
Reads a term from corpus/glossary/terms.jsonl and the owning glossary record beside it.
Answers a question about the corpus as a whole from corpus/reports/.
Reads an ADR from corpus/adrs/, says whether it is in force, and follows a supersession to the ADR now in force.
Reads an NFR from corpus/nfrs/: the target a service or an offering commits to, and whether it binds.
Reads an offering from corpus/offerings/: what a customer gets, and the services that deliver it.
Reads a postmortem from corpus/postmortems/, and fetches its timeline and actions through retrieval.md, because neither travels.
Reads a service from corpus/services/: what it does, its repositories, what it calls, and how its failure reaches a person.

Reviews a change in a forked subagent against views/review.md, read whole. It takes a rule's link from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl, and reads a control from corpus/controls/ where the export carries controls.
Generated by kac bundle from corpus/standards/rules.jsonl: every standard rule by title, under its standard's id and status, so a session about to write code can tell which rules to read.

Generated by kac bundle from corpus/standards/ and corpus/controls/: each standard rule's obligations and the controls checking it, for a reviewer to read in full. A corpus exporting no controls still gets it.

A SessionStart hook printing the breadcrumb rendered beside it, so a session learns the corpus is here before it has a question. A PreToolUse hook printing the build index at the first tool call of the main session and of each subagent, and again after a compaction, where views/build-index.md survived. They name no type, so they travel wherever a component reading one did.
